items.stem: A rise in arterial blood pressure is detected by the baroreceptors. Which immediate autonomic response restores pressure toward baseline?

options.text: Increased parasympathetic tone, lowering heart rate
options.rationale: Correct: baroreceptor firing raises vagal (parasympathetic) tone and reduces heart rate to lower cardiac output.

options.text: Increased sympathetic tone, raising heart rate
options.rationale: This would raise pressure further, worsening the disturbance.

options.text: Release of renin to retain sodium
options.rationale: Renin acts over hours to days, not as the immediate reflex.
Venoconstriction would raise, not lower, pressure.

items.explanation: Correct: baroreceptor firing raises vagal (parasympathetic) tone and reduces heart rate to lower cardiac output.

items.stem: A drug's hepatic clearance falls while dose and dosing interval stay the same. At steady state the plasma concentration will:

options.rationale: Correct: at a fixed dose rate, steady-state concentration is inversely related to clearance, so lower clearance raises it.
Lower clearance cannot reduce steady-state concentration at a fixed dose.
Steady-state concentration depends on clearance, so it changes.
The drug is still administered; concentration does not fall to zero.

items.explanation: Correct: at a fixed dose rate, steady-state concentration is inversely related to clearance, so lower clearance raises it.

items.stem: Which TWO features most directly distinguish a malignant neoplasm from a benign one?

options.rationale: Correct: local invasion is a defining feature of malignancy.
Correct: metastatic potential is characteristic of malignant tumours.
A capsule is typical of benign, not malignant, tumours.
Slow expansile growth is more typical of benign lesions.

options.text: Cells resembling the tissue of origin
options.rationale: Close resemblance (differentiation) is more typical of benign tumours.

items.explanation: Correct: local invasion is a defining feature of malignancy.
